name: Sodium Benzoate
whatItIs: Sodium benzoate is a synthetic sodium salt of benzoic acid widely used to prevent food spoilage.
whyAdded: Extends shelf life significantly and inhibits the growth of mould, yeast, and bacteria in acidic foods and beverages at very low cost.
bodyEffect: Processed safely by the liver in small quantities and excreted in urine. Can form trace benzene if combined with Vitamin C under heat.

name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
whatItIs: MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid naturally found in tomatoes, cheese, and mushrooms.
whyAdded: Intensifies umami (savory) flavor profiles in ultra-processed foods, making low-cost formulations taste richer and more satisfying.
bodyEffect: Digested like natural glutamate. Some sensitive individuals report mild transient flushing or headaches when consumed in high doses on an empty stomach.

name: Tartrazine (FD&C Yellow No. 5)
whatItIs: Tartrazine is a synthetic azo dye derived from petroleum that imparts a bright lemon-yellow color to foods.
whyAdded: Restores visual color lost during high-temperature manufacturing and creates bright, appealing visual identity in confectionery.
bodyEffect: Has been linked in European food studies to hyperactive behavior in sensitive children and rare allergic reactions (hives, asthma flare-ups).

name: Citric Acid
whatItIs: Citric acid is an organic acid naturally found in citrus fruits, produced commercially via fungal fermentation of molasses.
whyAdded: Provides a tart, sour flavor, balances sweetness, and acts as an antioxidant and natural preservative.
bodyEffect: Extremely safe; acts as an intermediate in human cellular energy production (Krebs cycle). High amounts may cause tooth enamel erosion.

name: Palm Oil / Palmolein
whatItIs: Edible vegetable oil derived from the mesocarp of the fruit of oil palms.
whyAdded: Provides high thermal stability for deep frying, resists oxidation/rancidity at room temperature, and gives crisp texture at a low manufacturing cost.
bodyEffect: High in saturated fatty acids (~50%), which can elevate LDL (bad) cholesterol levels when consumed regularly in large amounts.

name: High Fructose Corn Syrup / Invert Sugar
whatItIs: A liquid sweetener produced from corn starch that has been enzymatically processed to convert glucose into fructose.
whyAdded: Cheaper and sweeter than cane sugar, blends effortlessly into liquids, retains moisture in baked goods, and prevents crystallization.
bodyEffect: Metabolized predominantly by the liver. High consumption is strongly associated with insulin resistance, non-alcoholic fatty liver, and weight gain.

name: Potassium Sorbate
whatItIs: Potassium salt of sorbic acid, naturally occurring in some berries, manufactured synthetically for food use.
whyAdded: Inhibits molds and yeasts in a wide range of moisture-rich foods without altering taste or appearance.
bodyEffect: Breaks down in the body into water and carbon dioxide just like naturally occurring fatty acids; non-toxic and well tolerated.

name: Caramel Color IV (Sulfite Ammonia Caramel)
whatItIs: A dark brown coloring agent produced by heating carbohydrates in the presence of both sulfite and ammonium compounds.
whyAdded: Gives deep brown hue to cola drinks and gravies, maintaining consistent appearance across large production batches.
bodyEffect: Contains trace amounts of 4-MEI (4-methylimidazole), a byproduct formed during manufacturing. Regulatory agencies enforce strict safety limits.

name: Soy Lecithin
whatItIs: A mixture of phospholipids extracted from soybean oil processing.
whyAdded: Prevents separation of water and oil phases, improves flow of melted chocolate, and extends freshness in bakery items.
bodyEffect: A source of essential choline. Generally safe, though persons with severe soy allergies should exercise caution.

name: Xanthan Gum
whatItIs: A soluble polysaccharide produced by fermentation of glucose or sucrose by Xanthomonas campestris bacteria.
whyAdded: Increases liquid viscosity, prevents ingredient settling, and improves mouthfeel in low-fat or gluten-free products.
bodyEffect: Acts as a dietary soluble fiber. Excess consumption may cause mild digestive bloating or laxative effect.

name: TBHQ (Tertiary Butylhydroquinone)
whatItIs: A synthetic aromatic organic compound that acts as an antioxidant for unsaturated vegetable oils and animal fats.
whyAdded: Prevents rancidity and oxidation of fats in ultra-processed snacks, extending shelf life up to 1-2 years.
bodyEffect: High acute doses in animal studies showed potential cellular stress. Strictly regulated with maximum allowed limits in human food.

name: Hydrogenated Vegetable Oil (Trans Fat)
whatItIs: Fat produced by industrial hydrogenation of liquid vegetable oils into solid fats.
whyAdded: Provides solid structure at room temperature and long shelf stability for commercial baking at low cost.
bodyEffect: Significantly increases LDL (bad) cholesterol and decreases HDL (good) cholesterol, strongly raising cardiovascular disease risk.
